solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Support around Tory leader withdrawn by recorder of minutes (10)

indicatorNotes.around: the support wraps round the leader's name
indicatorNotes.withdrawn: withdrawn = drawn back, so the name reads backwards

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball; its letters open around the next piece
KEMI (Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservatives, or Tories) read backwards

annotation.surface: A politician's backing drains away after the party leader is dropped, all noted by the person taking the minutes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' reads as a meeting's written record, but the recorder here keeps time. 'By' is not a link: it supplies PER.
annotation.definitionFit: A timekeeper records the minutes and seconds of a race or match.

entries.clue: Adherent not having leader’s heart (6)

indicatorNotes.not having leader: the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a sticker is someone who sticks to a cause

annotation.surface: A follower who no longer has a party leader to follow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' is informal for the heart. The apostrophe-s is read as 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ticker is a slang word for the heart, from its beat.

entries.clue: Some agreements somewhat lacking (6)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the words is used, so the answer sits inside them

annotation.surface: A grumble that a set of deals falls rather short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like the indicator, but it is part of the letters: the answer starts in its last two.
annotation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity or quality.

entries.clue: Unit of storage (KB) technician recalibrated – and in French (7,7)

indicatorNotes.recalibrated: the letters are set up afresh in a new order

blocks.note: the two letters as printed, first half of the fodder
the word itself; with KB, twelve letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: An IT worker resetting a unit of computer storage measured in kilobytes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'unit of storage' sound like computer memory, with KB as kilobytes; the unit is a cupboard. A kitchen cabinet is also a leader's informal circle of advisers.
annotation.definitionFit: A kitchen cabinet is a fitted cupboard unit used for storage.

entries.clue: Underrate distance across Ukraine and Spain (9)

indicatorNotes.across: the distance stretches across the country code, holding it

blocks.note: UA is the international code for Ukraine; it goes inside to give EXTEN(UA)T
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

annotation.surface: Someone playing down how far it is across Ukraine and Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' here strings E on after the container, rather than joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To extenuate is to lessen the seriousness of something, making it seem less than it is.

entries.clue: Plant unlimited rice in time (5)

indicatorNotes.unlimited: without its limits, the first and last letters
indicatorNotes.in: the remaining letters sit in the other word

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
rICe without its outer letters, placed within the period of time

annotation.surface: An instruction to put down rice, without limit, in good time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb, sowing rice, but it is the noun: the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of heaths and heathers, a flowering plant.

entries.clue: Rock opera sacking old queen live at the opening (4)

indicatorNotes.sacking: sacking = throwing out, so ER is dropped
indicatorNotes.at the opening: only the first letter is used

blocks.note: ER = Elizabeth Regina; sacked from OPERA to leave OPA

annotation.surface: A rock opera fires its ageing star, a Queen tribute, on opening night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock opera' looks like one phrase; split it, and rock is the definition while opera is the raw material.
annotation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone, a kind of mineral or rock.

entries.clue: Caught trawling bait for unwary surfers (8)

indicatorNotes.Caught: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so the word is taken by ear

blocks.note: trawling is fishing with a net; the online scam is pronounced the same

annotation.surface: Someone caught out fishing with bait meant for surfers who are not paying attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' reads as arrested, but it means heard. The surfers ride the internet, not waves, and the bait is a fake email designed to steal passwords.
annotation.definitionFit: Phishing is the online fraud of luring users with deceptive messages to capture their details.

entries.clue: Support tabloids regularly (medium strictly observing the law) (8)

indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly = at even intervals, so the letters are taken at a steady every-other-one rhythm

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or chair
M = medium, as on clothes labels

annotation.surface: Backing the tabloid press as a matter of routine, as a psychic who obeys every rule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medium' sounds like a psychic or a mass-media channel beside 'tabloids'; it is just the size letter. The definition sits inside the brackets.
annotation.definitionFit: Legalism is strict adherence to the letter of the law.
annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a descriptive phrase for the noun: legalism is strictly observing the law.

entries.clue: Illicit trader‘s dodgy remark about character after dark (5-9)

indicatorNotes.dodgy: dodgy = unsound, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged word goes round the letter
indicatorNotes.after: this part comes after the colour

blocks.note: the letter T spelt out; it sits inside MARKE(TEE)R

annotation.surface: A shady dealer's off-colour comment about someone, made after nightfall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet, spelt as a word: TEE.
annotation.definitionFit: A black-marketeer trades illegally in scarce or controlled goods.

entries.clue: Follow The Daily T (5)

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, as is a char (charwoman)

annotation.surface: A plug for the Telegraph, nicknamed The Daily T: follow it.
annotation.walkthrough: The Daily T is what the Telegraph calls itself, but a daily is also a British cleaning woman, as is a char.
annotation.definitionFit: To chart something is to track or follow its course.

entries.clue: Briefly prioritise patients, admitting new bad back for testing (9)

indicatorNotes.Briefly: said briefly, a word is cut short, so its last letter is lost
indicatorNotes.back: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: TRIAGE (sort patients by urgency) without its last letter
N + ILL read backwards, then let into the shortened word

annotation.surface: Hospital staff rushing to sort patients and taking in a new case of bad back pain for tests.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad back' reads as a medical complaint, but 'back' is an instruction to reverse the N and ILL.
annotation.definitionFit: Trialling means putting something through tests.

entries.clue: Planet Normal initially chasing electronic material for Planet Normal mug? (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially = at the start, so only the word's opening letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of Normal, following E

annotation.surface: A promotion for merchandise from Planet Normal, the Telegraph's podcast, a branded mug.
annotation.walkthrough: Planet Normal is a Telegraph podcast. The definition describes what a mug might be made of: an earthen mug is made of fired clay, fitting for an Earth-themed show.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthen describes pottery made of baked clay, a material for a mug.
annotation.definitionNote: Earthen is an adjective; the definition phrase describes the mug's material.

entries.clue: Jointly entertain last couple to leave, dividing everyone’s drink (7)

indicatorNotes.to leave: the last couple leave the party, so the final two letters depart from the word
indicatorNotes.dividing: the result splits the other word in two

blocks.note: all = everyone; it is split AL…L
to co-host is to entertain jointly
COHOST loses its last two letters, ST; what is left splits the other word

annotation.surface: Two hosts at a party wait for the last couple to go home, then split everyone's leftover drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last couple to leave' pictures departing guests; it means the last two letters go.
annotation.definitionFit: Alcohol is drink in the sense of intoxicating liquor.

entries.clue: Henna blend fixes bleached highlights, for example (12)

annotation.surface: A hairdresser's note: a henna mix holds dyed streaks in place.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue lives in a hair salon, so 'fixes' reads as setting the colour; it is the builder's word, cements.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: bleached streaks are one of many ways to improve looks.

entries.clue: Admit fraud involving note, plainly falling short (4,5)

indicatorNotes.involving: the fraud wraps round what follows
indicatorNotes.falling short: the word stops a letter early

blocks.note: a con is a fraud; it goes round the rest, CO…N
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A confession that a scam involving a banknote was plainly not enough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests money beside 'fraud', but it is the musical note ME.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: coming clean is confessing, washing off the dirt of a secret.

entries.clue: Detached spray of lilac, endlessly charming brought inside (8)

indicatorNotes.spray: a spray scatters, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.endlessly: without an end, so the word's final letter is lost

blocks.note: NICE (charming) without its last letter, set among the rearranged flower letters

annotation.surface: A charming loose spray of lilac, brought indoors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Detached' looks like a flower snapped off the bush, beside 'spray of lilac'; it means emotionally cool.
annotation.definitionFit: Clinical means coolly detached and unemotional.

entries.clue: Son tearful for blanket (8)

annotation.surface: A child in tears, crying for his comfort blanket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blanket' is the adjective, as in a blanket ban: all-covering.
annotation.definitionFit: A sweeping measure is a blanket one, covering everything.

entries.clue: Left phoney war – teamwork indicated main retreat (3-5,4)

indicatorNotes.phoney: not genuine, so the letters are faked into a new order

annotation.surface: A history of the Phoney War, when joint effort on the left marked a retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: The Phoney War was the quiet first months of World War II; here 'phoney' is the indicator. 'Main' is the sea, and its retreat is the ebb tide.
annotation.definitionFit: The low-water mark shows how far the sea goes back at low tide.

entries.clue: Three characters following Golf – gang heading off to take over vehicle (6)

indicatorNotes.following: the letters that come after G in the alphabet

blocks.note: Golf is G in the NATO alphabet; H, I, J come next
PACK (a gang) without its first letter

annotation.surface: Three villains trailing a golfer, the gang's boss gone, set out to steal a car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' reads as people, but they are letters of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the phrase, though hijack is now used loosely of seizing anything, from meetings to accounts.

entries.clue: Looker’s light-hearted taking off top (6)

annotation.surface: A good-looking person being cheerful while taking off a top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Looker' suggests an attractive person; here it is an eye, the thing that looks.
annotation.definitionFit: Ocular means of the eye, the organ that looks.
annotation.definitionNote: Looker’s is a possessive, standing for the adjective 'of the eye'.

entries.clue: Lacking northern energy in grid originally absorbs Miliband (7)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally = at its origin, so only the first letter of grid is used
indicatorNotes.absorbs: a sponge absorbs water by taking it in, so the name goes inside the letters

blocks.note: E (energy) + IN + G, first letter of grid
Ed Miliband, the Labour politician; absorbed into E(ED)ING

annotation.surface: A northern power grid falls short, and Ed Miliband as energy secretary takes the blame.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container word but is just the letters IN; the container indicator is 'absorbs'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: if you are in need of something, you are without it.

entries.clue: Plough a nation contributing land (5)

indicatorNotes.contributing: the words each give part of the answer

annotation.surface: A call for farmers to till the soil for the good of the country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plough' and 'land' both suggest farming, keeping the country out of sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Ghana is a country in West Africa.

entries.clue: Oleic acid only half digested in someone avoiding gluten (7)

indicatorNotes.only half: just half the word is used
indicatorNotes.digested: broken down, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A diet note: a certain fatty acid is only partly absorbed by people on a gluten-free diet.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry and digestion make the clue read as nutrition advice, which hides that 'digested' means rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: coeliac disease is an immune reaction to gluten, so sufferers cut it from their diet.

entries.clue: One cry during lust in outburst of bad behaviour (5,4)

indicatorNotes.during: happening within, so the letters go inside

blocks.note: to lust is to crave; it goes round the rest, CR…AVE
a mew is a cat's cry

annotation.surface: Someone cries out in the heat of passion during a wild night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lust' is a verb here, synonym of crave, not a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A crime wave is a sudden rise in lawbreaking.

entries.clue: Trouble behind meme discovered in message (5)

indicatorNotes.discovered: dis-covered: its covering outer letters taken off

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble; it comes behind EM

annotation.surface: The trouble caused by a meme that turned up in someone's message.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as 'found' but means stripped of its cover.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: electronic mail is one kind of message, alongside letters and texts.

entries.clue: Device content from travelog ongoing (4)

indicatorNotes.content from: the contents of the phrase supply the letters

annotation.surface: A gadget stuffed with the text of a travel diary that keeps being updated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Device' reads as a gadget, but in heraldry and branding a device is an emblem.
annotation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or device identifying a brand.

entries.clue: Loan provider misused brawn in game (10)

indicatorNotes.misused: used wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: poker is a card game; it opens after its first letter to take the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A moneylender who used muscle in a card game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brawn' suggests a heavy collecting debts, fitting the moneylender, but it is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker lends money against goods left as security.
